statements.t: Senju completed Phase 2 and Phase 3 clinical trials of KIO-401 in patients with central retinal artery occlusion (“CRAO”) in Japan, and we plan to initiate a global Phase 3 registration trial in CRAO in 2027 and a Phase 2b clinical trial in non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (“NAION”).
We will pay Senju a $3.5 million upfront payment and may pay additional technology transfer, regulatory, commercial launch and sales milestones and royalties on net sales.

In the future, if the option is exercised and a license agreement is executed, we will be eligible to receive an additional $109.5 million plus tiered royalties of up to high teen percentages on net sales.
We will report data from patients enrolled in the KLARITY clinical trial and intend to pursue partnering or out-licensing opportunities for KIO-104.

We expect to incur significant expenses and increasing operating losses for the foreseeable future as we continue the development and clinical trials of and seek regulatory approval for our product candidates.

If we obtain regulatory approval for our product candidates, we expect to incur significant expenses in order to create an infrastructure to support their commercialization including sales, marketing, and distribution functions.
We will need additional financing to support our continuing operations.

We will seek to fund our operations through a combination of public or private sales of equity, debt financings, license and development agreements, non-dilutive grants and other sources, which may include collaborations with third parties.
We will need to generate significant revenue to achieve profitability, and we may never do so.

While we anticipate having sufficient cash to fund currently planned operations into late 2027, excluding the technology transfer milestone, we will need additional financing to support our future operations as we develop and work toward the commercialization of new products.
We have incurred losses and negative cash flows since inception, and future losses are anticipated.

Based on the cash on hand and short-term investments at September 30, 2026 of approximately $5.6 million and $10.7 million, respectively, the near term payment of $3.5 million due to Senju under the KIO-401 License Agreement and all KIO-301 expenses reimbursed by our partner TOI, we anticipate having sufficient cash to fund currently planned operations into late 2027, excluding the technology transfer milestone,…
We expect to continue to incur significant expenses and increasing operating losses for the foreseeable future.
We anticipate that our expenses will increase substantially if and as we:

Until such time, if ever, as we can generate substantial product revenue, we expect to finance our cash needs through a combination of equity offerings, debt financings, collaborations, strategic alliances, grants and licensing arrangements.

To the extent that we raise additional capital through the sale of equity or convertible debt securities, the ownership interest of our stockholders will be diluted, and the terms of these securities may include liquidation or other preferences that adversely affect the rights of holders of common stock.

Based on our cash on hand and short-term investments at September 30, 2026, we believe that we will have sufficient cash to fund planned operations into late 2027, excluding the technology transfer milestone, which may become payable prior to such date.
To continue development, we will need to raise additional capital through debt and/or equity financing, grants and other arrangements.
Accordingly, no assurances can be given that management will be successful in these endeavors.
The Company plans to report results from patients enrolled in the KLARITY study and evaluate partnering opportunities.

“Our current cash position enables us to fund pre-trial activities needed to prepare KIO-401 for its next stage of development, including CMC and regulatory work ahead of enrollment and dosing, when spending will increase,” said Melissa Tosca, CPA, Chief Financial Officer of Kiora.
We will continue to maintain a streamlined operation, aligning spending with development milestones.

risks.t: uncertainties associated with preclinical and clinical development and regulatory review
the possibility that results observed in previous studies will not be reproduced in future studies
the possibility that regulatory feedback will require changes to proposed trial designs, endpoints, follow-up periods or development timelines
the possibility that orphan drug designation will not be granted or that anticipated incentives or exclusivity will not be available
the cost, timing, enrollment, conduct and outcomes of clinical trials
the Company’s ability to maintain anticipated collaboration reimbursements and manage operating expenses
the ability to obtain sufficient capital to fund planned development activities
the availability and terms of future financings
the Company’s ability to execute its development strategy and licensing obligations
